question: Shops sold Pampers nappies at a steady rate. How did orders further up Procter & Gamble's supply chain behave?
options: Just as steady as the sales
Far more jumpy at each step
answer: Far more jumpy at each step. Distributors' orders to P&G swung more than shop sales, and P&G's orders to its own suppliers swung more still. Each stage read small blips as trends, batched its orders and hoarded when short. It is called the bullwhip effect: a flick at the handle, a crack at the tip.
move: Each layer that reacts to the one below adds its own noise.
trap: Expecting stock between the stages to absorb the ups and downs.
source: Lee, Padmanabhan & Whang, Sloan Management Review, 1997
reference: Lee, Padmanabhan & Whang, The Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains, Sloan Management Review 38(3), 1997
